intel.t: A logger and union man who owes nothing to Trump or billionaires, running against Collins as a reliable Trump vote; he says Trump gets her vote "100% of the time" when he needs it.

intel.l: Biggest vulnerability as opponents frame it
intel.t: His Augusta record on electric rates and taxes, the mortgage residency question, late disclosure, and $138K in personal union consulting pay; Collins also notes his past opposition to abortion.
Independents, 52 to 45 in Marist October 1 to 4, and voters who say Trump's policies hurt Maine's economy or oppose tariffs, per CBS and YouGov.
Four in ten Democrats wish someone else were the nominee, and Hannah Pingree runs ahead of him for governor.
His "Oh, shut up" line at the final October 15 debate in Bangor; the Maine GOP called it unacceptable.

bottom: Jackson became the nominee at a special Democratic convention in late July 2026, after Graham Platner left the race. Jackson had finished third in the June primary for governor, per the BDN on October 15, 2026, https://www.bangordailynews.com/2026/10/15/politics/elections/troy-jackson-fundraising-disclosure/. In his first quarter as nominee he raised $20.4 million, about four times what Collins raised, and spent $16.5 million. He entered October with $4 million in cash and about $1 million owed to a vendor.
Three interests combine money and a decision:
**Small donors.** ActBlue processed $17.1 million, about 90 percent of his individual receipts. The campaign says nearly 200,000 donors gave and 95 percent of gifts were under $100.

**Labor unions.** Unions are his PAC money and his paycheck. The Machinists paid him $90,000 and the Painters $48,000 as a consultant from March 2025 into 2026, through his run for governor. Both unions also gave his Senate campaign $5,000 each. The lever is labor law and NLRB confirmations.

intel.t: Seniority and results: the Appropriations gavel, federal money for Maine, and a record of independence, citing her effort against Hegseth.

intel.l: Biggest vulnerability as opponents frame it
intel.t: That she gives Trump the votes he needs, "100% of the time" in Jackson's words, plus the Navatek pay to play allegation she denies.
Repeat Collins voters and state focused voters; she wins about one in five Trump disapprovers and holds enough Democrats to tie, per CBS News and YouGov, September 23 to October 1.
At the final October 15 Bangor debate, Jackson told her "shut up" after she tied a protester to him; the Maine GOP called it unacceptable and she is using it in ads per a RedState headline not read.
Marist, October 1 to 4: Jackson 51, Collins 47 among registered voters; independents Jackson 52 to 45; 57 percent expect Collins to win.

bottom: Collins is being outraised by Troy Jackson and carried by outside money. She had raised more than $18 million by the end of June 2026, per Boston.com on October 15, 2026, https://www.boston.com/news/politics/2026/10/15/troy-jackson-tells-susan-collins-to-shut-up-during-heated-maine-senate-debate/. Groups backing her had booked about $126 million in ads through the end of the year, per the Bangor Daily News on October 19, 2026, https://www.bangordailynews.com/2026/10/19/politics/elections/massive-republican-money-web-susan-collins-campaign-joam40zk0w/.
Four interests combine money and a decision she controls:

**Senate Republican leadership.** SLF booked nearly $50 million in Maine. Its top donor nationally, One Nation, gave it $132.9 million and booked nearly $35 million of its own Maine ads. The decision is Senate control and her Appropriations gavel.

**Billionaires through Pine Tree Results PAC.** The super PAC closest to her is run by Scott Reed and funded by Stephen Schwarzman, Ken Griffin and two dark money nonprofits. New Balance owner Jim Davis gave $1 million to a Collins super PAC in 2025.

D.t: Troy Jackson leads by 2.6 in the forecast and wins 71% of simulations. The cushion is about 19,214 votes; a one point swing is about 3,709 voters changing sides.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between R +4.3 and D +9.1. A normal polling error decides it.
The polls page average is D +3.5. Your best recent poll is Echelon Insights for NetChoice at D +6.7; your worst is New York Times/Siena University at R +3.7. 19 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Cumberland, a projected net 65,861 votes; York, a projected net 8,418 votes; Knox, a projected net 3,244 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: York, D +7.2, 15.7% of the vote; Kennebec, R +8.3, 8.9% of the vote; Androscoggin, R +11.1, 7.1% of the vote; Hancock, D +9.1, 4.4% of the vote.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Troy Jackson runs furthest behind in Piscataquis, Aroostook, Somerset. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: White voters, 95% of voters, 50 to 48, where a 5 point gain is worth 4.75 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 77% of voters, 52 to 46, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.85 points; Voters without a degree, 60% of voters, 47 to 51, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.02 points.
The forecast's worst groups for Troy Jackson: Immigration voters 14 to 84, Men 43 to 55, Midsize counties 45 to 53. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
Registered Democrats cast 48% of the 244,931 ballots in Maine so far, against 22% for the other party. That is 0.3 points worse for Democrats than the forecast expected by now.

D.h: What the ballots so far say
D.t: The early vote has moved this forecast 0.4 points away from Troy Jackson. Election Day has to make it up: the remaining vote must break harder your way than the forecast expects.
Activity: 3 campaign stops by the candidate or surrogates in 30 days.

R.t: Susan Collins trails by 2.6 and wins 29% of simulations. Closing it takes about 9,607 voters switching sides, or 19,214 more net votes from new turnout.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between D +9.1 and R +4.3. A normal polling error decides it.
The polls page average is D +3.5. Your best recent poll is New York Times/Siena University at R +3.7; your worst is Echelon Insights for NetChoice at D +6.7. 19 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Republicans: Penobscot, a projected net 13,777 votes; Aroostook, a projected net 11,985 votes; Somerset, a projected net 9,509 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: York, D +7.2, 15.7% of the vote; Kennebec, R +8.3, 8.9% of the vote; Androscoggin, R +11.1, 7.1% of the vote; Hancock, D +9.1, 4.4% of the vote.

R.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
R.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Susan Collins runs furthest behind in Cumberland, Hancock. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: White voters, 95% of voters, 48 to 50, where a 5 point gain is worth 4.75 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 77% of voters, 46 to 52, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.85 points; Voters without a degree, 60% of voters, 51 to 47, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.02 points.

The forecast's worst groups for Susan Collins: Large counties 30 to 68, Health care and Social Security voters 32 to 66, Corruption voters 33 to 65. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
Registered Republicans cast 22% of the 244,931 ballots in Maine so far, against 48% for the other party. That is 0.3 points better for Republicans than the forecast expected by now.

R.h: What the ballots so far say
R.t: The early vote has moved this forecast 0.4 points toward Susan Collins. Bank it: chase the remaining mail ballots and low propensity voters who have not voted.

media.what: Ran a Morning Meeting segment on Maine's evolving Democratic Senate field and the deadline for Graham Platner to exit the race.
Called Maine the Senate tipping point state, with Troy Jackson narrowly ahead of Susan Collins in his polling error test.
At a Princeton talk he called Susan Collins's seat the most obvious Democratic Senate opportunity.
Ran a segment on a report about Democratic candidate Graham Platner's alleged past behavior and relationships.
Mocked the Maine Democratic Senate debate and its candidates' policies and discussed the effect on Susan Collins.
Called the Collins vs Platner race a contest with no clear leader in his Senate math segment.
In a YouTube forecast video listed Maine as a Democratic lead of 3 points on the path to a Democratic sweep.
Anchored The Briefing live from Portland, Maine, focused on Collins vs Troy Jackson.
Contrasted Republican reaction to the Platner allegations with GOP silence on allegations against Trump.
Said Maine is in play and will be close but Collins is a survivor.
Devoted an episode to Graham Platner's campaign against Susan Collins the morning after the Maine primary.
